objectives: LO 1.1.1: Identify what financial intermediaries do, especially investment bankers and dealers
LO 1.2.1: Identify the parts, terms and mechanics of primary and secondary markets (orders, short sales, margin)
LO 1.3.1: Recognize the features and tax treatment of each type of cash or cash equivalent
LO 1.4.1: Assess how capital gains and losses, dividends and wash sales affect an investor's taxes
synthesis: This module is the plumbing of investment planning: how securities are born (underwriting), where they trade (primary vs. secondary markets), how trades are executed and financed (orders, margin, short sales), and what the client keeps after tax. Cash equivalents anchor the emergency fund and supply the risk-free rate used in later return and portfolio models. The tax rules here (netting, wash sales, qualified dividends, NIIT) drive asset location and tax-loss harvesting decisions in every client review.

example.title: Harvesting a loss without tripping the wash sale rule
example.html:
Fictional client Mara has a $12,000 net long-term gain this year from selling a fund. She also holds 300 shares of Pine Co. with a $21,000 basis now worth $15,600.

  1. Sell Pine: $15,600 − $21,000 = −$5,400 short-term loss (held under a year).
  2. Cross-net: $12,000 LT gain − $5,400 = $6,600 net LT gain taxed at 0/15/20% (2026 edition figure) instead of $12,000.
  3. If she rebuys Pine within 30 days before or after the sale (2026 edition figure), the loss is disallowed and her new basis becomes the repurchase cost + $5,400.
  4. Option: wait 31+ days, or hold something similar but not the same meanwhile.

keyNumbers: $500,000 per customer, max $250,000 cash (2026 edition figure)
$3,000/yr net; excess carried forward indefinitely (2026 edition figure)
More than 60 days in 121-day window (2026 edition figure)
3.8% × lesser of NII or MAGI over $250K MFJ / $125K MFS / $200K other (2026 edition figure)
mustKnow: Firm commitment: underwriter bears unsold shares; best efforts: issuer does
Stop → market order (execution certain); stop-limit → limit order (price certain)
Margin-call price = loan per share ÷ (1 − maintenance %)
Liquid ≠ marketable: MMDA is liquid only; T-bill is both
T-bill income: federal ordinary income, state-exempt; munis: federal-exempt, state-taxable unless in-state
Netting: ST with ST, LT with LT, then cross-net; $3,000 cap on net loss
Wash sale: disallowed loss is added to the replacement shares' basis
traps: Using the original purchase price (not current price) when computing a margin deposit
Forgetting the short seller pays dividends to the share lender
Calling a money market mutual fund FDIC-insured (only MMDAs are)
Treating REIT or S corporation dividends as qualified
Thinking the wash-sale window only looks forward from the sale
tips: Margin HPR: divide by the investor's own money and subtract margin interest
NIIT: always compare NII to MAGI over the threshold and tax the smaller
For I/II/III/IV items, eliminate any combination containing one false statement first
